messages:
Mia Chen: quick heads-up — starting bring-up for cetus-corp LoRA merge on int4 today, running the quick eval pack now. will share initial numbers when ready.

Arjun Patel: good call. FYI we saw a small amount-handling drift in a different customer on int4 last month — keep an eye on currency/invoice tokens. :eyes: 

Mia Chen: noted. running `smoke-eval-v2 --pack cetus --quant int4` now. expected runtime ~3m.

qa-bot: smoke-eval started (id: smoke-1832). tests: basic-likelihoods, number-extraction, safety-checks, latency.

Mia Chen: pasted first short report: 
```
--- smoke-1832 summary ---
BLEU: baseline_fp16 0.123 -> int4 0.121
Amount-exact-match: 99.3% -> 95.6%  <-- concerning
p50 latency: 86ms -> 68ms
topk-token-shift (mean): 0.4% -> 1.9%
KV-cache load ok, no OOMs
```

Priya Rao: 95.6% on amounts is a regression we shouldn't ship for invoices. do we know if it's tokenizer aliasing or quant rounding?

Mia Chen: digging in. initial diff of token probs shows systematic downshift on tokens like "USD", "€", and numeric separators. snippet: 
```
context: "Total: USD 12.34 due"
fp16 probs: [USD: -2.1, 12: -1.3, .34: -3.0]
int4 probs: [USD: -3.6, 12: -2.8, .34: -5.9]
```

Liam O'Connor: hmm that's classic scale mismatch in the last layer quant params. did you try per-channel calibration or outlier clipping during quant?

Mia Chen: ran per-tensor int4 quant with our default symm calibrator. next I'm spinning a per-channel clip run + OP-level bias correction. also testing a small fallback rule: for tokens matching currency regex, use fp16 route (model variant).

Arjun Patel: fallback route sounds reasonable short-term. can we quantify perf cost? how many requests would hit fallback for cetus workloads (they're invoice-heavy).

Priya Rao: asked cust-eng for sample traffic mix. in parallel, let's run a targeted eval with 5k invoice prompts to estimate hit-rate. Mia, can you queue that as `eval-invoices-5k`?

Mia Chen: queued `eval-invoices-5k` (job 1832-INV). running per-channel int4 and a hybrid int4+fp16 fallback where we patch token mask for currency tokens. ETA ~12m.

qa-bot: job 1832-INV started. retaining full logs to S3: <https://s3.redwood-internal/cetus/1832-inv/logs>

Deploy-bot: canary deploy for `cetus-int4-v1` scheduled to pool-7 in 10m unless blocked.

Arjun Patel: hold the canary until we see invoice eval. if fallback rate >5% or amount-acc drop >1.5% vs fp16 we block.

Mia Chen: results in 11m: 
```
--- eval-invoices-5k ---
per-channel-int4 amount-exact-match: 96.1%  (delta vs fp16: -3.2%)
hybrid (int4 + fp16-currency-fallback) amount-exact-match: 99.0% (delta -0.3%)
fallback-hit-rate: 7.8% of requests
latency p50 hybrid: 75ms (vs int4-only 68ms)
```

Priya Rao: hybrid looks like it restores accuracy but fallback-hit-rate 7.8% > 5% threshold. need cost/latency tradeoff decision from product / cust-eng.

Liam O'Connor: technical notes: fallback implementation is straightforward (token-mask => route to fp16 variant) but increases tail latency when requests hit fallback due to model switch. we can reduce hit-rate by tuning quantization clipping thresholds or doing a small 8-bit activation calibration on those currency token positions. recommend trying: 1) per-channel clipping + bias correction 2) lightweight activation int8 for last layer 3) hybrid as fallback.

Mia Chen: I'll run per-channel + bias correction test next (job 1832-CH). if that gets amount-acc >98.8% and fallback <4% we can proceed with canary.

Arjun Patel: assign action items: @Mia Chen run 1832-CH and 1832-LASTINT8; @Priya Rao coordinate with cust-eng for cost acceptance if fallback stays ~7-8%; @Liam O'Connor prepare quick patch PR for hybrid routing and metrics.

Priya Rao: pinged @cust-eng-cetus for traffic mix and commercial approval.

Mia Chen: thanks. I'll post updates in this thread. ping me if you want the raw prob diffs or the eval notebooks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deferred for `cetus-int4-v1` (blocked: invoice-accuracy regression).
